sections.h2: Where do Northampton County deeds get recorded?
sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds works from Room L116 of the county government center at 669 Washington Street in Easton. Phone 610-829-6210. The counter is open from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., except that any recording needing a parcel certification stops at 4:00 p.m.

The division records, images and stores deeds, mortgages and other real estate papers filed in the county. Each document gets a volume and page reference, then it is imaged and made available for viewing and copying. It also collects the fees and taxes on property transfers and passes them along.

For anyone selling a house in Northampton County, this is the last stop on closing day. The deed is signed at the title company, delivered here, and the recording puts the buyer's name in the public record. A late afternoon delivery after 4:00 p.m. can slip a day if the deed needs a parcel certification, which most do.

sections.h2: What are the Northampton County recording fees?
sections.html:
A deed costs $76.25 to record under the schedule effective December 1, 2025. That covers up to four pages and four names, and parcel certification is charged on top.

Northampton County recording fees, effective December 1, 2025
DocumentFee
Deed$76.25
Mortgage$76.25
Assignment or release of mortgage$61.75
Satisfaction of mortgage$61.75
Easement or right of way$59.75
Power of attorney$18.50
Parcel certification, per parcel$10.00
Each page over four, each name over four$2.00, $0.50

Source: the Recorder of Deeds fee schedule published on the county website. A power of attorney for the sale of real estate costs the same $18.50 but also takes the parcel certification.

The schedule adds a few smaller lines: a Statement of Value costs $2 and counts toward the page total, certifications cost $2.50, and copies are $0.50 a page.

sections.h2: How should a closing agent pay the Northampton County recorder?
sections.html:
Checks go out to the Recorder of Deeds, and the county says no personal checks. It takes business checks, certified checks, money orders or cash. No more than five documents can ride on one check.

The office wants the exact amount with each document and will not accept an overpayment. That detail trips up closing packages built from a rough estimate, so the amount should be worked out line by line from the schedule above.

  • Count the pages first, then add the $2 for every page past four.
  • Add $10 for each parcel on documents marked with an asterisk on the schedule.
  • Count names past four at $0.50 each.
  • Add the separate transfer tax payment if the deed is taxable.

sections.h2: Which paper rules does the Northampton County recorder enforce?
sections.html:
The schedule opens with its house rules, and they decide whether a deed is recorded or returned.

  • Parcel numbers must appear on every document that relates to real estate. The county points filers to its public parcel search at ncpub.org.
  • The largest accepted page is 8.5 by 11 inches. A document that does not fit, limited to 8.5 by 14, pays a $10 penalty.
  • Blanket assignments, releases and satisfaction pieces are refused.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope with enough postage must come with any document sent back by mail.

The page count matters because the fee is built on it. A deed with a long legal description and an attached exhibit can pass four pages quickly, so check before you assume the base price.

sections.h2: How does transfer tax work on a Northampton County sale?
sections.html:
The recorder collects the state's 1 percent realty transfer tax, along with any local tax the municipality and school district levy. Pennsylvania's Department of Revenue says the buyer and the seller are jointly liable for it.

Some transfers escape the tax, including certain transfers between family members, deeds to governments, and property passed by will or intestate succession. A seller who thinks a family deed qualifies should say so to the title agent early. Ask the Northampton County Recorder of Deeds for the local rate that applies in the municipality where the house stands, since local shares differ across the county's cities, boroughs and townships.

The sales contract is where buyer and seller agree who pays it, so read that clause before closing day.

sections.h2: What does Northampton County look like to a seller?
sections.html:
Northampton County sits in the Lehigh Valley, with Easton as the county seat and Bethlehem as the largest city. It was formed in 1752 from part of Bucks County and covers 377 square miles. The Delaware River forms its eastern edge, and the Lehigh River runs through it.

Heavy industry shaped it. Bethlehem Steel was based in Bethlehem until it was dissolved in 2003, and the region also made cement. The Census Bureau estimated 324,411 residents in 2025.

Housing costs sit well below Montgomery County to the south. Census figures for 2020 to 2024 give a median owner-occupied value of $308,600, median household income of $89,184 and an owner-occupied rate of 71.1 percent. The county adopted a home rule charter in 1978, with a county executive and a council.

sections.h2: Which Northampton County municipalities send deeds to this office?
sections.html:
All of them. The county has two cities, Bethlehem and Easton, plus a long list of boroughs and townships, and every deed for land inside the county line is recorded in the same Easton office no matter where the house stands.

The largest places by the 2010 census were Bethlehem at 74,982 people, a city that spills partly into Lehigh County, then Easton at 26,800, Bethlehem Township at 23,730, Palmer Township at 20,691 and Forks Township at 14,721. Smaller boroughs include Northampton, Wilson, Hellertown, Nazareth, Bangor, Pen Argyl and Wind Gap.

That matters on a sale for two reasons. A house in Bethlehem may sit on the Lehigh County side of the city, which is a different county and a different recorder, so confirm the county before you plan the closing. And local transfer tax and school district bills follow the municipality, so a seller in Hellertown and a seller in Palmer Township can see different closing figures on the same $300,000 sale.

sections.h2: What should I check before a Northampton County closing?
sections.html:
Most delays are paper problems, not legal ones. Work through the list a few days ahead.

  • Confirm the parcel number on the deed matches the county's parcel search.
  • Count pages and names to get the exact fee, with no overpayment.
  • Ask whether the title company will deliver by 4:00 p.m., since parcel-certified recordings close early.
  • Pull the tax certification and any unpaid tax before the closing date.
  • Ask the title agent how the Statement of Value is being counted in the page total.
  • Collect a return envelope with correct postage if the deed is coming back by mail.

Open mortgage balances get released through a satisfaction piece, which costs $61.75 to record. Ask the lender how long it takes to file one so the buyer's title is clean.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Northampton County?
faqs.a: The recording fee for a deed is $76.25 for up to four pages and four names. Add $10 for each parcel certified, $2 for each page past four and $0.50 for each name past four.

faqs.q: Does the Northampton County recorder accept personal checks?
faqs.a: No. The schedule says business checks, certified checks, money orders and cash are accepted, and no more than five documents can go on one check.

faqs.q: Can I overpay the recording fee in Northampton County?
faqs.a: No. The office requires the exact fee with every document and does not take overpayments, so the total should be calculated before the package is delivered.

faqs.q: When does the Northampton County recorder stop taking documents?
faqs.a: The office is open until 4:30 p.m., but recordings that require parcel certification end at 4:00 p.m. A deed delivered after that time will wait for the next business day.

faqs.q: Who pays Northampton County realty transfer tax when a house is sold?
faqs.a: State law makes buyer and seller jointly liable for the 1 percent state tax. The sales contract decides who actually pays, so check that clause.
